question: Does a Problem Commons packet improve independent solver understanding and contribution entry relative to a credible ordinary challenge brief built from the same underlying problem facts?

ordinary_brief.description: Same title, observed condition, unresolved goal, scope, constraints, authority boundary, success criteria, and workstream descriptions; omits explicit evidence/uncertainty/frontier/capability/stage/governance organization.

problem_packet.description: Minimum-necessary redacted Problem Packet plus explicit uncertainty/evidence context and safe stage/governance enrichment.

assignment: Deterministic counterbalancing by problem_id + participant_id for pilot convenience; preregister/replace with a formal randomization plan before confirmatory claims.

interpretation.minimum_sessions_for_nontrivial_pilot_re: At least 5 sessions per arm; still exploratory, not inferentially confirmatory.
do_not_claim: causal product impact from uncontrolled sessions
generalization across domains from a single problem

failure_signals: Problem Packet arm does not improve comprehension or time-to-useful-edge despite materially greater curation burden.
Problem Packet needs more coaching than the ordinary brief.
Solver serious-attempt conversion is no better or worse after repeated cases.
Participants report that stage/governance/frontier structure adds ceremony without changing their work choice.
Control/treatment cannot be kept fact-equivalent without hidden curator judgment.
